test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
What grammatical function does the phrase "utilizing wooden rails to minimize friction" serve in the sentence?

"Early prototypes, such as horse-drawn wagon ways in 16th-century Europe, represented rudimentary precursors to modern trains, utilizing wooden rails to minimize friction and facilitate the movement of goods..."

options.text: Gerund phrase acting as the subject

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Adverbial phrase explaining the manner**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"utilizing wooden rails to minimize friction"** modifies the verb **"represented"** by explaining how the action was performed.
 
• Such phrases function adverbially, providing information about the manner or means of the action.
 
• It does not modify a noun (so it is not an adjective clause), nor does it function as a subject or an object in the sentence.
 
• It answers the question **how** the prototypes functioned as precursors to modern trains.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective clause:** Would begin with a relative pronoun like "which" or "that" and modify a noun. This phrase does not do that.
 
• **Noun clause:** Typically acts as a subject or object and starts with words like "that" or "what." This is not the case here.
 
• **Gerund phrase acting as the subject:** Would appear at the beginning as the main subject, e.g., "Utilizing wooden rails was important." In this sentence, the phrase explains how something was done, not what did it.
